entryPoint: SLA::addGracePeriod(Datetime $date, BusinessHoursSchedule $schedule = null, &$timeline = array()) in include/class.sla.php
coreLogic: SLA::addGracePeriod's own body performs the calculation: schedule resolution via ($schedule ?: $this->getSchedule() ?: $cfg->getDefaultSchedule()), then delegates working-hours math to BusinessHoursSchedule::addWorkingHours($date, $this->getGracePeriod(), $timeline) (include/class.schedule.php), which wraps BusinessHours::addWorkingHours($date, $hours, &$auditlog) (include/class.businesshours.php) for the real business-hours walk and timeline population; when no schedule resolves, the fallback is a plain DateInterval add of round($this->getGracePeriod()*3600) seconds directly on $date.
consumers: Ticket::getSLADueDate() in include/class.ticket.php (line 558): builds $dt from getReopenDate() ?: getCreateDate() in DB timezone, calls $dt = $sla->addGracePeriod($dt, $schedule) where $schedule = $this->getDept()->getSchedule(), then re-applies DB timezone to $dt and returns $dt->format('Y-m-d H:i:s') as the ticket's est_duedate. This is the only real call site found in the codebase (excluding orchestrator/pipeline tooling references and .kody rule examples, which merely document the seam, not call it).
inputShape: Datetime $date (by-reference object, mutated in place, required); BusinessHoursSchedule $schedule = null (optional explicit schedule override); &$timeline = array() (optional by-reference array, populated with a human-readable diagnostic log of the working-hours walk when a schedule path is used — left as the default empty array on the plain-hours fallback path). Implicit inputs: $this->getGracePeriod() (SLA's grace_period property, in hours, float/numeric), $this->getSchedule() (lazy-loaded via SLA's schedule_id), and global $cfg->getDefaultSchedule() (system default schedule, lazy-loaded).
outputShape: Returns the same DateTime instance passed in as $date, advanced in place to the computed due date; the method's own return value is a convenience alias to the same mutated object (not a new one) — callers typically capture it as $dt = $sla->addGracePeriod($dt, ...) but the mutation is visible on the original reference regardless. If a schedule is used and BusinessHoursSchedule::addWorkingHours succeeds, $timeline is also populated by reference with the audit log from BusinessHours::getTimeline().
sideEffects: Reads global $cfg (osTicket config singleton) to call $cfg->getDefaultSchedule() when no explicit or SLA-local schedule is available; this lazily loads and caches $cfg->defaultSchedule via BusinessHoursSchedule::lookup($cfg->getDefaultScheduleId()), a DB read on first access.
SLA::getSchedule() lazily loads and caches $this->_schedule via BusinessHoursSchedule::lookup($this->getScheduleId()) — a DB read on first access per SLA instance.
Mutates the input $date DateTime object in place (advances it to the due date) rather than returning a new object.

Mutates the by-reference $timeline array parameter when the schedule path is taken, overwriting it with BusinessHours' internal timeline log (via BusinessHoursSchedule::addWorkingHours -> $timeline = $bhrs->getTimeline()); left untouched (default empty array) on the no-schedule fallback path.
BusinessHours::addWorkingHours (invoked transitively) calls $date->setTimezone($this->getSchedule()->getDatetimeZone()) as a side effect, changing the DateTime's timezone before computing offsets.

BusinessHours::initOccurrences (invoked transitively per work-hours iteration) reads schedule entries and holiday schedules via getSchedule()->getEntries() / getHolidaysSchedules(), each a DB-backed lazy collection walk.
constraints: Schedule precedence must be preserved exactly: requested $schedule parameter first, then SLA's own getSchedule(), then the system default $cfg->getDefaultSchedule() as final fallback.
If a resolved schedule's addWorkingHours() call returns a truthy value (a DateTime), that value must be returned immediately — the plain-hours fallback below must NOT run in that case.

If no schedule resolves at all (all three precedence sources are falsy), OR if the resolved schedule's addWorkingHours() call returns falsy (e.g. schedule has zero entries per BusinessHours::addWorkingHours's own guard), execution must fall through to the plain-hours fallback: $date->add(new DateInterval('PT'.round($this->getGracePeriod()*3600).'S')).
The grace period hours value must come from $this->getGracePeriod() (SLA::grace_period), consistently in both the schedule path and the fallback path.
$date must be mutated in place and returned as the same reference both in the schedule-success branch and the fallback branch — callers may or may not capture the return value.
$timeline is populated by reference only along the schedule-success branch; the fallback branch does not touch it, and its default value stays array().

Method signature (parameter types, optionality, and by-reference $timeline) must remain byte-for-byte identical after extraction so existing callers (notably Ticket::getSLADueDate) keep working unchanged.

The extracted service must not call back into SLA::addGracePeriod() (anti-recursion) — it should hold the lifted schedule-precedence/fallback expression itself and forward-delegate only to BusinessHoursSchedule::addWorkingHours / BusinessHours, never to the facade entry point.

Facade-level orchestration (the global $cfg lookup, SLA-local schedule resolution via $this->getSchedule(), and the overall precedence chain) is facade-level side effect logic per the repo's strangler rule — the smallest correct extraction lifts the core precedence+fallback calculation into the service while class.sla.php keeps owning access to $cfg and $this.
harnessInputShape: JSON object with: start (string, ISO 8601 datetime); hours (number, grace period hours — use 0 for guard cases); schedule_id (integer, BusinessHoursSchedule id — 1 for normal business-hours schedule, 5 for empty-schedule fallback testing)
